question:
I have recently upgraded dbt to 1.1.1 version but I am facing an issue where when I run dbt compile for a single model it is throwing multiple push notifications on duo which wasn't the case earlier in my local virtual environment setup. For one model it used to send only one push notification before dbt upgrade. I do not wish to remove MFA completely but can someone please provide any information on how to handle this scenario. What are the best practices on using MFA to connect to snowflake from DBT?

Regards Ashsc
title: Using MFA after DBT upgrade to version 1.1.1 to connect snowflake
answer:
1. In your DBT Project, open your profiles.yml file and add authenticator: username_password_mfa to your appropriate target environment (e.g., dev).
  2. In your Snowflake account, run alter account set allow_client_mfa_caching = true.

The DBT documentation for Snowflake references this and says:

Along with adding the authenticator parameter, be sure to run alter account set allow_client_mfa_caching = true; in your Snowflake warehouse. Together, these will allow you to easily verify authentication with the DUO Mobile app (skipping this results in push notifications for every model built on every dbt run).

I had this same issue once I enrolled in MFA for my Snowflake account. I had previous been able to execute dbt run, without MFA for my user, but the first time I did this after enrolling in MFA I was hit with over 30 DUO Push notifications.
